post.caption:
Uranus kept missing its predicted position, so Le Verrier and Adams independently calculated the mass, distance and position of an unseen planet pulling on it. Berlin Observatory pointed a telescope at the coordinates and found Neptune within an hour, one degree from the prediction. The same method's failure case is just as interesting: Mercury's drift led Le Verrier to predict a planet called Vulcan. It does not exist. Gravity itself was different from what he assumed.
